Multi-select is built and I've smoke-tested it in a browser (bulk tag, select-all, archive all worked; only a harmless favicon network 404). Try it on the sample set: **[http://maker:4001/?seed=1](http://maker:4001/?seed=1)**.

👉 **1. Click "Select"** (top-right of the list). Checkboxes appear and a dark **action bar** slides up at the bottom.

👉 **2. Tick a few bookmarks** (click anywhere on a card to toggle it). The bar shows how many are selected.

👉 **3. Click "+ Tag,"** type a tag, and apply — it's added to all the ones you picked. Try **"– Tag"** too: it lists the tags on your selection so you can strip one from all of them.

👉 **4. Try "Read later," "Mark read," and "Archive"** on your selection and watch them update together.

👉 **5. The filtered-action case:** click **"Cancel select"** to exit, then **search `#reading`** (or click a tag). Now click **"Select"** again and hit **"Select all N matching."** Any action you run now applies to **exactly those matching bookmarks and nothing outside that filter.** Then clear the search and confirm the others were untouched.

👉 **6. Click "Delete"** with some selected — you get the same **named confirmation** as single delete, covering the whole batch.

Decisions I'd like your reaction to:
- **How selecting works:** a dedicated "Select" mode with checkboxes (rather than checkboxes always cluttering every card). In that mode, tapping a card selects it instead of opening it. Does that feel right on both computer and phone?
- **"Select all N matching"** is how you act on an entire search/view at once — it deliberately never touches bookmarks outside your current filter, exactly as you asked.
- **Archive vs Restore** in the bar swaps automatically depending on whether you're in the Archived tab.
